Description: Metrics tracking populations, abundance, diversity, or extinction risk of species
Metrics on extent, condition, or change in ecosystems and land cover
Benefits provided by nature — provisioning, regulating, cultural
Drivers of biodiversity loss (pollution, land change, climate, overuse)
Monetary or quantified economic value of natural capital and services
Measures tracking governance, protected areas, restoration actions

No relevance to climate or weather. The calculation is based entirely on administrative records, GIS area measurements, or financial data. Examples: protected area extent, certification area, expenditure data.

Theoretically affected by climate as a background driver, but climate/weather data are not used in the calculation. Examples: habitat condition from field surveys, conservation status assessments, cumulative INNS counts.

Climate or weather data are used indirectly within underlying models, or inter-annual weather variability is a known and significant confounder of the indicator value. Examples: bird population indices (BBS counts affected by spring weather), fish stock assessments (SST in productivity models), pollinator occupancy models.

Weather or climate data are a direct, explicit input to the calculation methodology, or the indicator is specifically designed to measure a climate-related biological response. Examples: butterfly abundance indices (weather-corrected flight activity), wintering waterbird counts (cold-weather movements), Spring Index (explicitly regressed on temperature), bat activity counts (temperature thresholds), climate vulnerability index (uses climate projections as primary input).

Apply with the scale above. Written after a cross-sheet harmonisation found three readings of the scale in use (data dependency; 'climate is a threat driver'; 'relevant to climate policy'). Only the first is the scale. Review record: outputs_other/climate_score_harmonisation/climate_score_harmonisation_proposal.xlsx.

Score the measured quantity as published: do weather or climate data enter its calculation, and does inter-annual weather materially move its value? Do NOT score topical relevance to climate policy (Policy_Sector = Climate carries that), the policy purpose of the measure (e.g. that it is an adaptation measure), or the fact that climate change is a long-run driver of the thing measured.

Administrative, financial, legal, GIS-boundary, deployment/installed-capacity, certification and count-of-plans measures score 0 - including those whose subject is climate (NDCs, DRR strategies, adaptation plans, climate finance, carbon-credit registries, assets 'assessed and adapted').

Status assessments and extents from mapping or field survey, where climate is a recognised driver but no climate data enter and weather does not materially move the annual value, score 1: Red List Index and all its disaggregations, Red List of Ecosystems, STAR, phylogenetic-diversity loss, conservation status, habitat/site condition, INNS counts, land-cover and habitat extent (incl. mangrove, saltmarsh, seagrass, forest), connectivity derived from land cover. Exception: reef-building corals RLI scores 2 (assessments rest on climate-driven decline).

Emissions inventories (activity x emission factor), emission intensities, and energy demand or intensity score 1. A temperature-adjusted (weather-corrected) series scores 3. LULUCF and ecosystem carbon-flux estimates from models that take temperature or rainfall score 2.

Quantities that inter-annual weather moves materially, or that are modelled with climate data indirectly, score 2: survey-based population indices (BBS, LPI, WBI), occupancy models for insects, fish stock assessments, plankton and trophic indices, measured or modelled air-pollutant concentrations, renewable-generation shares, water demand, leakage and abstraction compliance, surface-water extent, harvest volumes and yields at national scale, disease and pest incidence.

Score 3 when (i) weather or climate data are a direct, explicit input (temperature adjustment, fire-weather index, reanalysis soil moisture, climate projections as primary input, DGVM/remote-sensing NPP driven by meteorology); (ii) the quantity is itself a physical climate-system or hydrological variable (temperature, sea level, ocean heat, pH, river flow, groundwater level, reservoir storage); (iii) the quantity is defined by attribution to weather or climate events or thresholds (heat-attributable mortality, weather-event disruption or loss, return-period standards, overheating thresholds); or (iv) it is designed to measure a climate-related biological response (phenology, butterfly/moth flight-activity indices, thermal community indices).
Composites: score the component that defines the headline quantity; where a climate-defined component is a named part of the measure, it governs.
The same measured quantity on more than one sheet takes one score, unless the source methodology genuinely differs - and then the rationale says how.
Targets (IFW-10) are scored on the quantity the target is expressed in, not on the target being an adaptation target.
